name: FactSet
key_signal: FDS trades near 40% below its 52-week high at just 13x forward earnings, but earnings growth is actually contracting (-9.6%) even as the stock bounces off a technical low.
thesis: At 13.1x forward earnings and 17x trailing, FDS is priced well below its historical premium multiple for a recurring-revenue data/analytics business with 51% gross margins, 30% operating margins, and 27% ROE. The stock has stabilized and turned higher — up 8.6% over 21 days and 11.9% over 63 days, now trading above both its 50- and 200-day moving averages with a positive MACD histogram — suggesting the selloff from the $432 high may be exhausting itself. Low beta (0.72) and a 1.8% dividend add defensive characteristics while the market waits for earnings growth to reaccelerate from the current 6.4% revenue growth base.
bear_case: Earnings growth is negative (-9.6%) even as revenue growth has slowed to just 6.4%, meaning margins are compressing or one-time items are hurting profitability — this is the real reason the stock is down ~40% from its highs, not just multiple compression. The 126-day momentum of -11.7% shows the stock was in a sustained downtrend for most of the past six months, and the recent bounce could simply be a dead-cat rally within a broader de-rating as FactSet faces intensifying competition from Bloomberg, S&P Capital IQ, and cheaper AI-driven data alternatives that threaten its per-seat pricing model. With 16 analysts already covering the name and a consensus 'hold' rating, there's little informational edge left to exploit, and debt-to-equity of 77% limits flexibility if earnings continue to soften. The lack of a golden cross (50dma still below 200dma) signals the longer-term trend has not yet confirmed a reversal.
